title: KV preservation & long-context kernel experiments - lab notes
content:
Purpose / quick summary:
This is a scratchpad for the KV preservation problem with long contexts: when sequences exceed a certain length (observed ~65k tokens in our tests), the KV layer sometimes returns stale values or the attention kernel selector picks a non-matching kernel and we see token hallucinations / coherence breaks. Collecting commands, logs, repros, and hypotheses here so we can triage without losing breadcrumbs.

What I was chasing (high level):
- Repro of misaligned KV reads after long prefix + streaming decode.
- Whether kernel selection (sparse/dense/fused attention) boundary decisions are correlated with the glitch.
- If there is an integer wrap/offset in KV indexing (modulo, eviction pointer, or bucket rollover).

Environment:
- runtime branch: feature/kv-longcontext-experiments (local)
- binary: serving-runtime:v0.33.1-rc (built locally with debug symbols)
- model: open-llama-3b-v1 (config: n_ctx=131072, kv_shard=8)
- hardware: 1xA100-80GB, driver 535, cuda 12.1
- quant: q4f16 experiment enabled in config but tests run both quant and float
- test harness: local harness (python harness/repro_long_kv.py)

Short reproduction notes (commands I ran):
1) baseline that usually succeeds:
   PYTHONPATH=. pytest tests/test_kv_preserve.py::test_kv_simple_prefix -q

2) longer sequence repro (failed intermittently):
   python harness/repro_long_kv.py --prefix-file=tests/data/long_prefix_60k.txt --gen-len=512 --seed=42

3) stress run (looping) to catch flakiness:
   for i in $(seq 1 200); do python harness/repro_long_kv.py --prefix-file=tests/data/long_prefix_60k.txt --gen-len=512 --seed=$i || break; done

Observed behaviors / logs (snippets - redacted):
- Typical successful run ends with: "decode complete, kv_hits=98.7%, avg_kv_latency=1.2ms"
- Failed run snippet (from runtime stdout):
   [2024-10-27 11:23:45] WARN attention: selected kernel=fast_block_sparse for seq_len=65544 (expected fused_unfused)
   [2024-10-27 11:23:45] ERROR kv-cache: read_mismatch at global_idx=65536 expected_key_digest=0x7f3a got=0x0000 (len=64)
   [2024-10-27 11:23:45] ERROR decode: coherence_break detected at token_idx=65553 (token: "the")
- In one run I saw a sequence of repeating tokens (loop) starting right after the kernel selection WARN.
- Kernel selection logs: we have a tiny selector that currently does: if seq_len <= threshold_map[kernel] then pick kernel; there is rounding in the mapping (we store threshold as float and cast to int late). Suspect off-by-one.

Quick bisect attempts / experiments and results:
- Change 1: force kernel selection to "always_dense" for seq_len > 32768
  - result: no failure in 200 runs. Suggests kernel switching might be involved.
- Change 2: disable prefix cache eviction (treat KV as append-only) via env KVCACHE_EVICT=0
  - result: failure rate dropped but not eliminated. Failures that remain have different offsets (not always at same global_idx).
- Change 3: change hash digest length in KV to 16-bit (temporary) to see collisions
  - result: no new collisions, so reported 0x0000 entries are not simple digest collisions.
- Change 4: add assert after KV read: if key_digest == 0 -> dump last 256 keys and abort
  - result: dump shows valid digests earlier but at indexes around 65536 we see an all-zero block in raw backing buffer. Suspect mmap/zeroing or wrap.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Off-by-one in kernel threshold cast: selector uses float thresholds (e.g., 65536.0) but the runtime cast path sometimes yields 65544 and picks the wrong kernel -> downstream read path expects different strides/indexing -> misread.
2) KV backing store buffer index uses signed 32-bit index somewhere (or 16-bit in some path) and wraps at 65536 (2^16) causing an apparent zeroed region. Evidence: failures cluster at multiples of 65536.
3) Async page allocator / ring buffer alignment: when we cross a page boundary the allocator zeros a page that overlaps the KV buffer due to off-by-one in allocation size.
4) CUDA kernel variant (fast_block_sparse) uses a different KV layout (packed vs strided) and code path incorrectly assumes one layout -> memory aliasing.

More detailed notes on hypothesis 2 (wrap/overflow):
- I grepped for any uses of uint16_t or int32 in kv_layer.* and found a helper that stores local_offset as uint16_t in older code paths. That helper is used by the packed-serializer path which sometimes gets invoked by the sparse kernel.
- If local_offset rolls over at 65536 we would observe the zero-block symptom.
- Patch idea: change local_offset -> uint64_t in serializer + add invariant checks.

What I tried to validate the wrap hypothesis:
- Instrumented: add runtime check that logs type/size of offset variables in hot path (printf) and observe in failing runs. Observed one log where local_offset printed as "-1" (signed print) before crash.
- Recompiled with -fsanitize=undefined (where possible) - a few builds failed due to toolchain but one run produced an out-of-bounds write in serializer.cpp:line 312.

Commands + patches I executed:
- quick patch that changes serializer::local_offset from uint16_t -> uint64_t and rebuild
   git checkout -b fix/kv-offset-width
   edit runtime/kv/serializer.h (local_offset uint64_t)
   make -j8 && ./bin/runtime --run-smoke-tests
  result: reduces failures by ~70% in short stress (50 runs) but still some intermittent fails.

Attention kernel notes (why kernel could matter):
- Kernels expect KV buffer layout to be either interleaved per-head (for fused) or contiguous (for fused_unfused). If selector picks the wrong kernel the kernel will index wrong strides and produce incorrect attention weights leading to incoherent decoding.
- Selector heuristics currently: consider seq_len, model_size, last_cache_hits. There's a race where last_cache_hits is updated asynchronously. If the selector uses slightly stale last_cache_hits combined with floating threshold rounding it can flip kernel choice at large seq lens.

Repro artifacts I captured:
- failing dump: /tmp/kvdump_fail_20241027.tar.gz (contains kv raw buffer at time of fail, last 512 keys, kernel_choice.log, decode_trace.log). (local only)
- saved a minimal input that reproduces on my machine: tests/data/min_repro_65536.txt

Open questions / things to try next (concrete):
- Force kernel to fused_unfused for long sequences and run large regression (500+ runs) across both quant and float. If completely eliminates failure => kernel mismatch is root cause.
- Add strong invariants/asserts in KV serializer: bounds checks on every read/write, explicit type widths. Keep them gated under env debug to avoid perf impact.
- Audit everywhere we store offsets/lengths for use of uint16_t/uint32_t vs uint64_t. Grep for "uint16_t" in runtime/kv and runtime/attention.
- Re-run with ASAN/MSAN on CPU path or cuda-memcheck for CUDA kernels to catch out-of-bounds in kernels.
- Small test harness: create artificially padded prefix lengths around 64k boundary (65500..65570) and run deterministic seeds to see whether failure correlates with exact length or kernel boundary.

Notes to self (less formal):
- Benji thinks kernel selector change last week was safe but he updated thresholds; ping him for threshold_map history.
- Ellen suggested that page-size alignment bugs are plausible because allocator recently switched to 2MB huge pages. Double-check /proc/meminfo and jemalloc config.
- Keep reproducer minimal: dropping the model size to 1b can still reproduce — good for faster loops.

Immediate todo (this sprint):
- [ ] Add gated asserts to serializer (Ayesha)
- [ ] Run 500-run kernel-forced experiment (Benji)
- [ ] Grep & audit type widths (Ellen)
- [ ] Create small CI job (nightly) that fuzzes prefix lengths around 64k boundary (Ayesha + infra)

If I get a few minutes: instrument kernel selector to log both the float thresholds and the cast int thresholds at selection time. That will either confirm rounding/OBO issue or point elsewhere.

End of scratchpad.

-- A.K.
